criteria.criterion: Production lines of crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (everything before the first #[cfg(test)] module) are fewer than 1500. Check by Grep for '^#\[cfg\(test\)\]' with line numbers in drain.rs and reading the first match; the line before it is the production line count.
criteria.evidence: Grep for '^#\[cfg\(test\)\]' found the first match in drain.rs at line 1193, so there are 1192 production lines (< 1500). The CHANGELOG states the same 4585 → 1192.

criteria.criterion: New files under crates/athena-cli/src/drain/ (at least lifecycle.rs, real_steps.rs, lander.rs, engine.rs) each have fewer than 1500 production lines, checked by Grep for line numbers of the first #[cfg(test)] or the file length via Read.
criteria.evidence: None of the drain/ files has a #[cfg(test)] line. File lengths from the diff stat (all-addition new files): engine 620, item_work 1042, lander 200, lifecycle 582, real_steps 574, rounds 422. Each is under 1500.

criteria.criterion: The diff (git diff) only moves code, adds mod and re-export lines, and adjusts imports or visibility such as pub(super). No function body logic changes, and crate::drain public paths used by main.rs and display.rs (guarded, DrainState, StopOutcome, RestartOutcome and others) remain exported from drain.
criteria.evidence: The drain.rs hunk is '@@ -1179,3405 +1179,12 @@', one contiguous deletion of the production block. Its 12 added lines are 6 `mod`, 4 `pub use` (engine, lander, lifecycle, real_steps) and a 2-line comment. I compared each new file with the old drain.rs (git diff --numstat on the two file versions). Lines that match nothing in the old file: lander 3, engine 71, item_work 40, rounds 18, lifecycle 9, real_steps 9. pub(super) counts per file: 1, 69, 27, 11, 7, 7. Each file also has a 3-line header (doc comment, `use super::*;`, blank line). The rest (about 10 lines) fits the extra impl header and closing brace from splitting the Drain impl, plus reordering. I could not read each of these lines: the full colored diff was saved outside the working directory and reading it was denied. main.rs and display.rs are not changed, `cargo build` succeeds, and the drain tests pass, so the public paths still resolve.

criteria.criterion: No test is deleted, ignored or edited beyond import paths: the #[cfg(test)] modules stay in drain.rs (or move with their code) with the same test function names. Check with git diff and Grep for '#\[test\]' counts before and after.
criteria.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1 --stat -G#\[test\]` printed nothing, so no #[test] line was added or removed anywhere. The only drain.rs deletion is the production block, which ends before the old first test module at line 4586. All five test modules (batches_tests, tests, in_flight_tests, read_ahead_tests, landing_queue_tests) are still in drain.rs at lines 1194, 1249, 2311, 2422 and 3388.

findings.summary: Two created files are not on the expected deliverables list: drain/item_work.rs and drain/rounds.rs.
findings.evidence: The diff stat shows crates/athena-cli/src/drain/item_work.rs (1042 lines) and drain/rounds.rs (422 lines) as new files. These are harmless and not logic changes, but the sentence is not literally complete.

summary: The candidate passes. It splits drain.rs into six child modules: engine, item_work, rounds, lander, lifecycle and real_steps. drain.rs now has 1192 production lines, down from 4585, which meets the under-1500 goal. Every new file is under 1100 lines and none contains test code. The drain.rs diff is one contiguous deletion of the production block (old lines 1179 to 4583). The only lines added there are 6 `mod` lines, 4 `pub use` lines and a 2-line comment. The test modules are unchanged and no `#[test]` line was added or removed. main.rs and display.rs are untouched and the whole workspace builds. `cargo test -p athena-cli drain` passes: 71 lib, 3 main-binary, 1 binary.rs and 31 tests/drain.rs tests. Athena's CI record shows fmt, clippy and the full test suite passing. I compared each new file with the old drain.rs: 162 lines across the new files and drain.rs don't match the old file. 122 of these are `pub(super)` visibility edits; 18 are the new files' doc, `use super::*;` and blank lines; 12 are the drain.rs lines above. That leaves about 10, which fits the split impl headers and reordering. I could not read each of those last lines, because the full diff was saved outside the working directory and reading it was denied. There are two minor findings. First, the producer split the engine into three files (engine, item_work, rounds), so two files are outside the deliverables list; this was needed to keep each file under 1500 lines. Second, the CHANGELOG entry slightly understates the edits.
